chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died without having performed the Hajj of Islam, and he had wealth, he said: A 'sarurah' (female slave or dependent woman) performs Hajj on his behalf, if she has no wealth of her own.

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The first obligatory Hajj performed in one's lifetime
key_terms.صَرُورَةٍ: A female slave or a dependent woman under the care of a master

ai.seo_question: Who performs Hajj for a deceased person who died without wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain clarifies the financial liability for Hajj al-Muta'ah (Hajj of the deceased) by distinguishing between the deceased's estate and the performer's personal wealth. It establishes that a dependent woman (sarurah) may perform the ritual on behalf of the deceased using his funds, even if she lacks independent means, highlighting the Shia juristic view that the obligation rests on the deceased's assets rather than the agent's personal capacity. This ruling underscores the principle of vicarious performance in Shia fiqh when the primary obligation was neglected due to death.
